name: Parakeet Auklet
rangeDescription: North pacific and bering sea; winters to japan and southern california
description: Dumpy, medium-sized alcid with a bright orange bill. Pale button eye and upturned gape give it a distinctly maniacal, smiling appearance.

name: Laysan Duck
rangeDescription: Laysan island (northwestern hawaiian islands)
description: Highly range-restricted duck with a splotchy white “comma” around each eye. Found only on the Midway Islands, where it is the only resident duck.

name: Fork-tailed Pygmy-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (rio de janeiro, southern minas gerais, and northeastern são paulo)
description: Tiny flycatcher with a very distinctive head pattern and tail. Best field marks are the cinnamon head and the long, forked white-tipped tail framed by a dark border.

name: Gola Malimbe
rangeDescription: Humid forest of sierra leone, liberia, and southwestern ivory coast
description: A striking black-and-yellow malimbe; the female lacks the yellow nape of the male. Juvenile has a pale bill and yellow on the crown and chin.

name: Banded Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Northern australia (broome, western australia to cape york peninsula)
description: Small black-and-white honeyeater found in drier woodlands of northern tropical Australia. Black above, white below, with neat white cheeks and black breast band.

name: Yellow-bellied Sunbird-Asity
rangeDescription: Rainforest of east-central madagascar
description: Tiny, round, short-tailed yellow-bellied bird with a thin curved bill. Males are blue on the back and have bright bare skin around the eye in breeding plumage.

name: Blue-capped Hummingbird
rangeDescription: Southern mexico (sierra de miahuatlán of oaxaca)
description: Endemic and distinctive, medium-sized hummingbird found in the foothills of the Sierra Madre del Sur in Oaxaca. Favors humid evergreen forests and shade-coffee plantations.

name: Gray's Grasshopper Warbler
rangeDescription: Northeastern asia; winters to philippines, indonesia, and western new guinea
description: An odd, thrush-like warbler; extremely shy and seldom seen as it lurks about in dense undergrowth. The largest grasshopper-warbler, with a distinctly robust appearance.

name: Kashmir Nutcracker
rangeDescription: Eastern afghanistan (northeastern paktia and nuristan), northern and western pakistan (fort sandeman northward along suleiman range, chitral, gilgit, and baltistan), kashmir (sind valley, kishtwar, and badrawar), northwestern india (eastward to lahul, in himachal pradesh), and possibly adjacent extreme southwestern xizang (western china)
description: A jay-like bird with a long pointed bill, a black cap, and white spots all over. Very similar to Eurasian Nutcracker, but the Kashmir Nutcracker appears whiter overall with more white on the back, underparts, undertail, and tail tips.

name: Taiwan Rosefinch
rangeDescription: Mountains of taiwan
description: Endemic to Taiwan's mountain forests, this is the only breeding rosefinch on the island. Male deep wine-red with a frosty white brow and dark wings.

name: Royal Cinclodes
rangeDescription: Andes of southern peru and far western bolivia (la paz)
description: Medium-sized dark brown bird with a restricted range. Chunky and relatively long-tailed, with a reddish wing contrasting with its dark chocolate brown body, and a white eyebrow and cheek stripe.

name: Collared Laughingthrush
rangeDescription: Vietnam (langbian plateau)
description: Halloween-themed laughingthrush: decked out in black, gray, and orange. Combination of black head, silver ear patch, orange neck and breast, and multicolored wings are unmistakable in range.

name: Pompadour Cotinga
rangeDescription: Eastern colombia to southern venezuela, the guianas, northeastern bolivia, and amazonian brazil
description: Medium-sized, plump bird of rainforest canopy. Spectacular male is unmistakable, with shimmering pure white wings visible at a great distance.

name: Cardinal Lory
rangeDescription: Lowlands of bismarck archipelago and solomon islands
description: A thick-bodied, long-tailed parrot with entirely red plumage. The head appears slightly brighter than the body.

name: Orange-cheeked Honeyeater
rangeDescription: West-central new guinea (timberline zone of snow mountains)
description: A fairly large honeyeater of upper montane and subalpine forest and shrubbery. Overall olive color, light streaking with paler grayish belly and yellow legs.

name: Long-tailed Tapaculo
rangeDescription: Andes of colombia to ecuador and far northern peru
description: Small, mouse-like bird of Andean cloud forest. Often looks all gray in the dark forest understory it inhabits, but it does have rusty lower underparts with dark barring.

name: Tschudi's Tapaculo
rangeDescription: Central andes of peru (eastern la libertad to junín)
description: Small tapaculo of high-elevation cloud forest in the eastern Andes of northern and central Peru. Male is uniformly gray; female is paler and browner with extensive buffy barring.

name: Antioquia Brushfinch
rangeDescription: Northern central andes of colombia (antioquia)
description: Rare and endangered brushfinch thought to be possibly extinct until its rediscovery in 2018. It is only known from a few locations in the Colombian Andes north of the city of Medellín.

name: Mongolian Ground-Jay
rangeDescription: Desert of central asia (kazakhstan to outer and inner mongolia)
description: With its long, slightly decurved bill, flashy black-and-white wings, and ground-loving behavior, this bird is far from a typical jay. Sandy brown overall with a black crown and a thin dark line behind the eye.

name: Bahama Woodstar
rangeDescription: Varied habitats in bahamas (except for inagua group) and the caicos islands
description: A small, long-tailed hummingbird of wooded and scrubby habitats including gardens; most often found feeding on flowers or at hummingbird feeders. Note the male’s iridescent purple throat and forehead and its long, forked tail.
